## When to start

- The season in months: programs open in November, most close between mid
  January and early February, first offers go out in late February and early
  March.
- What to do in October and November so January is not a scramble.

## Where applications go

- NSF ETAP, the shared portal most NSF REU sites use, and what one account
  covers.
- Programs with their own forms, and national lab programs such as SULI.

## What goes in an application

- The personal statement and the research interest statement.
- Transcripts, and what a program can and cannot tell from a GPA.
- The list of courses and skills.

## Letters of recommendation

- Whom to ask, how early, and what to send them.
- How letters work when you apply to ten programs.

## Choosing where to apply

- How many programs, and how to read a project list.
- Programs for first and second year students, and for community college
  students.
- Programs abroad, and programs open to students who are not U.S. citizens.

## After offers go out

- The common early March reply deadline at domestic NSF physics REU sites.
- Waitlists, and what to do if you hear nothing.
